questions.q:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'

In practice rounds, my caddie, Greg, /and me works on my short/ game with a baseball glove.
o: and me works on my short
In practice rounds, my caddie, Greg,
questions.s:
There is are two errors in the part in option (a). First, we need to replace the objective pronoun 'me' with subjective pronoun 'I' as it is the part of the subject of the sentence.

Also, the subject 'Greg and I' is plural in nature. So, singular verb 'works' should be replaced with plural verb 'work'.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.q: May I know (1)/ to who (2)/ I am speaking ? (3)/ No error. (4)
questions.s:
After a preposition like “to”, we use the objective case of the pronoun → “whom,” not “who.”

questions.q: That is the book whose publication was delayed due to printing issues.
o: That is the book
delayed due to printing issues
questions.s:
In the sentence, "whose" is used to indicate possession or ownership. However, according to the rule provided, for non-living things, "whose" is not typically used. Instead, "of which" or similar construction is used to indicate possession.

So, the corrected sentence would be: "That is the book the publication of which was delayed due to printing issues."

questions.q: Either Rohan or Mohit (a) / has to prove their (b) / innocence before them. (c) / No error (d)
o: has to prove their
questions.s:
Either...or refers to one person at a time, so the pronoun must be singular — his, not their.
Correct sentence: Either Rohan or Mohit has to prove his innocence before them.

questions.q:
Everyone are very well equipped with his own weapons.

questions.s:
The sentence "Everyone are very well equipped with his own weapons" is grammatically incorrect.

"Everyone" is a singular subject, so the verb should be "is" instead of "are."

"His" is used for a singular male subject, but in this case, "everyone" refers to a group of people in general, so the possessive pronoun should be "their" to make it gender-neutral.

Correct sentence: Everyone is very well equipped with their own weapons.

Swami Vivekanand's vast knowledge of Eastern and Western culture appealed to all those who come in contacts with him.

questions.q:
I am sorry of which my mother said.

[MTS 06/07/2022 S3]
questions.s:
Correct Answer: for what

  • Corrected Sentence: I am sorry for what my mother said.

  • "Sorry for" is the correct phrase, as "sorry" is typically followed by "for" to indicate the reason for the apology.

  • "What" is used as a pronoun here to refer to the thing (in this case, the thing that the mother said). It refers to something that has already been mentioned.

questions.q: Identify the pronoun form of the words quoted -All of "those" are expensive.
questions.s: Those" is a demonstrative pronoun used to point out or identify specific things that are at a distance (plural form). Demonstrative pronouns include this, that, these, and those. Here "those" is pointing to specific expensive items. It's not a personal pronoun (like he, she, they) or an indefinite pronoun (like some, any, all).

questions.q:
Select the option that will improve the given sentence by using the most appropriate pronoun.

Pradeep, whom is a teacher, also works as a content writer.
o: Pradeep, which is a teacher, also works as a content writer.
Pradeep, whose is a teacher, also works as a content writer.
Pradeep, who is a teacher, also works as a content writer.
Pradeep, that is a teacher, also works as a content writer.
questions.s:
Correct answer is "who is." "Who" is the correct pronoun for a person, and "is" agrees with the singular subject "Pradeep."

Which is: "Which" is used for things, not people.

Whose is: "Whose" is possessive, not appropriate here; it needs a noun (e.g., "whose book").

That is: While "that" can sometimes be used for people, "who" is more appropriate for a person in this context.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).
